data.hypothesis: Keep explicit rsqrtf-based inverse-distance arithmetic, adding one Newton refinement step to its estimate, while restoring target-mass multiplication and final division. The prior globally cancelled mass path failed one protected case at N=16384; preserving those operations should avoid that risk while the refined reciprocal square root may improve numerical agreement. The extra refinement work may offset some speedup, so this remains a correctness-gated performance hypothesis.
data.notes: No local commands or measurements were run. The prior uncancelled rsqrtf candidate was valid and measured faster than baseline; the globally cancelled candidate failed one protected correctness case. This candidate changes the inverse-square-root arithmetic and retains target-mass operations. Require full correctness across all protected cases before official-size timing; no speed claim is made for this candidate.
transformations: Replace the direct rsqrtf estimate with one guarded Newton refinement step using fmaf; retain the positive softening term and self-interaction skip.
Restore target.mass multiplication in each force scale and divide accumulated force by target.mass after the source loop.
